chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud, the mawla of Abi al-Mi'za, from one who informed him, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman who menstruates, then the time of her purity passes while she still sees blood. He said: She should exercise precaution by waiting one day, if her menstruation is less than ten days. If the blood continues after ten days, then she is a mustahadah. If the blood stops, she performs ghusl and offers salat (prayer).

key_terms.الدَّمَ: the blood being observed in the ruling discussed
key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she waits an additional precautionary day before determining the ruling
key_terms.طُهْرِهَا: her state or period of ritual purity after menstruation
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: ten days; the upper limit relevant to distinguishing hayd from istiḥāḍah
key_terms.مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ: a woman in the state of istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman whose menstrual bleeding continues past her usual time of purity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman whose bleeding continues beyond the expected period of menstruation. It explains the rule of istiẓhār for one day when the hayd is under ten days, and clarifies that if bleeding continues beyond ten days, the ruling changes to istiḥāḍah, after which ghusl and salat (prayer) apply when the blood ceases.
